parts.name: operations-handbook.md
parts.body:
# Sample Housing Cooperative Operations Handbook

This handbook explains how the sample housing cooperative runs day-to-day operations. It is written for new committee members and staff. Every name in it is invented.

Version 3.2 — reviewed in October 2026.

# 1. Roles and Responsibilities

The cooperative has three standing committees. Each committee meets once a month and reports to the board.

## Board

The board sets the annual budget, approves contracts over the spending limit, and hires the operations manager.

## Maintenance Committee

The maintenance committee plans repairs, reviews requests, and keeps the contractor list current.

## Membership Committee

The membership committee runs the waiting list, welcomes new members, and handles move-outs.

# 2. Handling a Repair Request

Use these steps for every request, even small ones:

1. Log the request in the maintenance tracker within one working day.
1. Assign a priority:
  1. High: no heat, no water, a safety risk, or a door that will not lock.
  1. Medium: a fault that affects daily use.
  1. Low: anything else.
1. Book a contractor or a volunteer.
1. Confirm the fix with the member and close the request.

## Emergency Contacts

Out of hours: call the on-call line listed on the notice board.

- Water or gas leak: shut the valve first, then call.
- Lift fault: call the lift contractor.
- Fire: leave the building and call emergency services.

# 3. Spending Limits

The operations manager may approve spending up to the limits below. Anything above a limit goes to the board.

| Category | Single item limit | Monthly limit | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Routine repairs | €500 | €3,000 | Two quotes over €250 |
| Cleaning supplies | €150 | €600 | Use the approved supplier |
| Emergency work | €2,000 | No limit | Report to the board within 48 hours |
| Office costs | €100 | €400 | Keep all receipts |

Limits are reviewed each January. The next review is in January 2027.

# 4. Records

Keep signed contracts for seven years. Keep repair photos for two years. Store both in the shared drive under the year and the building name.

# Maintenance Committee Minutes

Date: 14 October 2026. Location: the common room.

Present: chair, treasurer, two volunteers, and the operations manager. Apologies: the secretary.

Seven requests are open. Two are high priority: the dead outlet in the annex and the radiator in the south building, which is fixed now.

The heating contractor will service both boilers in the first week of November. Members get two days’ notice before each visit.

The list has eleven contractors. The committee removed one roofing firm after two missed visits.

## Actions

Next meeting: 11 November 2026.

parts.name: visitor-policy.md
parts.body:
Sample Housing Cooperative

# Visitor and Guest Policy

This policy explains how members host visitors and overnight guests. It applies to all three buildings.

## Day Visitors

Members may host day visitors at any time. Visitors must leave the common room by 22:00 .

## Overnight Guests

A member may host an overnight guest for up to 14 nights in any 90-day period. Longer stays need written approval from the [membership committee](/committees/membership.html) .

- Tell the front desk the guest’s name and dates.

- Guests may not use the laundry room alone.

- Parking: guests use the visitor bays only. Bays V1 to V4 are in the north lot. Bay V5 is kept for deliveries.

### Approval Steps

- Fill in the guest form.

- Send it to the membership committee.

- Wait for the written reply, usually within five working days.

## Shared Spaces

| Space | Guests allowed | Booking |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Common room | Up to 10 | Book at the front desk |
| Roof garden | Up to 6 | No booking |
| Guest suite | 2 per night | Book online, €25 per night |

Route for guests: front desk, then the common room, then the guest suite.

![Ground floor plan](media/visitor-policy-image-001.png)

[Mermaid diagram source](diagrams/visitor-policy-mermaid-001.mmd)

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Member --> Form --> Committee --> Reply
```

## Questions

Ask at the front desk or email [desk@example.org](mailto:desk@example.org) .

Last updated 2 October 2026. Policy owner: membership committee.

parts.name: faq.md
parts.body:
# Frequently Asked Questions

### Can I paint my walls?

Yes. Use a light color, and return the walls to white when you move out.

### Who fixes a broken appliance?

The cooperative fixes appliances that came with the home. Report the fault through the maintenance tracker.

### Can I sublet my home?

No. Subletting is not allowed under the lease.

parts.name: guides-getting-started.md
parts.body:
# Getting Started

Welcome to the cooperative. This guide covers your first two weeks.

## Your First Day

- Collect your keys and fob from the front desk.

- Read the house rules in your welcome pack.

- Test the smoke alarm in your home.

## Your First Two Weeks

Register any pets, set up your monthly charge payment, and come to a welcome evening. The membership committee will contact you to arrange a short visit.

parts.name: guides-paying-charges.md
parts.body:
# Paying Monthly Charges

Monthly charges cover the cost of running the buildings. They are due on the first day of each month.

| Home size | Monthly charge | Repairs reserve share |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Studio | €610 | €45 |
| One bedroom | €780 | €60 |
| Two bedrooms | €945 | €75 |

## Late Payments

If you cannot pay on time, tell the treasurer before the due date. The cooperative can agree a payment plan.

parts.name: annual-report-summary.txt
parts.body:
Annual Report Summary 2025–26
Sample Housing Cooperative · Prepared for the annual general meeting
Overview
The cooperative ended the year with all 64 homes occupied and a small operating surplus.
Members voted to keep monthly charges flat for a second year. The board thanks the
volunteers who gave more than 1,900 hours of their time.
Membership
Nine households moved in and seven moved out. The waiting list grew to 112 households, the
longest it has been since the cooperative opened. The membership committee ran four
welcome evenings and one open day.
TwonewmembersjoinedtheboardinMarch.Trainingfornewboardmembersnowrunsover
threeeveningsinsteadofone.Year-roundsupportcomesfromamentorontheboard.
Finances
Income from monthly charges was €612,400. Spending was €598,150, so the surplus was
€14,250. Most of the surplus goes to the repairs reserve, which now holds €186,000.
Energy costs fell by 9% after the boiler upgrade in the south building. Insurance rose by 6%.
Looking Ahead
Next year the cooperative will replace the north building’s roof, add bicycle storage, and review
the visitor policy. The board will report on progress at each quarterly members’ meeting.

parts.name: pet-policy.txt
parts.body:
Sample Housing Cooperative — Pet Policy
Pet Policy
This policy sets out which pets members may keep and how to keep them without disturbing
neighbours. It applies to every home and to all shared spaces.
Pets Allowed
Members may keep up to two cats or one dog per home. Small caged animals and fish do not
need approval. Any other animal needs written approval from the board.
Approved by the board on 3 June 2026
Page 1 of 3
Sample Housing Cooperative — Pet Policy
Registration
Register each cat or dog with the front desk within two weeks of moving in or getting the pet.
Bring proof of vaccination. The front desk keeps the register and shares it only with the
maintenance team when they need to enter a home.
Shared Spaces
Dogs must be on a lead in all corridors, lifts, and the courtyard. Pets are not allowed in the
common room, the laundry room, or the roof garden, except for assistance animals.
Approved by the board on 3 June 2026
Page 2 of 3
Sample Housing Cooperative — Pet Policy
Complaints
If a pet causes repeated noise or damage, the membership committee will first talk with the
member. If the problem continues, the committee may ask the board to withdraw approval.
Review
The board will review this policy every two years.
Approved by the board on 3 June 2026
Page 3 of 3
